summary: Pietro Zullo, co-founder of Manufact (YC S25), presents MCP Apps as the official extension of the Model Context Protocol that allows MCP servers to return interactive UI elements rendered in sandboxed iframes within host chat applications. The talk traces the protocol's evolution: MCP launched in 2024; MCPUI was initiated by co-founder Idel Solomon in May 2025; and by January 2026 MCPUI became the official MCP Apps extension, with stores on Character AI and Claude opening at end of 2025. Manufact's open-source MCPUs SDKs have 8M+ downloads and 10K GitHub stars, with Manifold Cloud for shipping MCP servers. The core architecture has the host owning tools, the MCP server returning a widget in a sandboxed iframe, with bidirectional JSON-RPC-over-postMessage communication. Key primitives include set state (updating model context from UI without a user message), UI message (widget sends follow-up messages back into the conversation), incremental streaming UI updates, tool calling from widgets, and data redaction (showing rich UI while sending only sanitized data to the model). Display modes include inline, fullscreen with overlaid chat input, and picture-in-picture. Minor primitives support opening external links and OS theme synchronization. Live demos show MCP apps in Cursor (Pulsar analytics), Claude (Excalidraw streaming mermaid diagrams), and ChatGPT (Manifold analytics with better rendering). Client support spans ChatGPT, Claude (Co-work, Desktop), Cursor (agent mode, side chat), VS Code, and others. Builders detect client capabilities via metadata to conditionally return UI elements. MCPUs SDK lets developers return React widget components from the resources folder, compiled to HTML/CSS. Distribution uses self-serve stores on ChatGPT, Claude, and Cursor with submission involving tool scanning, authentication checks, and testing. One-click install URLs replace JSON config sharing. Claude currently performs dynamic discovery—searching the MCP registry for the right connector when no specific tool matches—with ChatGPT expected to follow. In closing, Pietro extends Paul Graham's observation that 'AI apps are the new browsers' by arguing Google Search is already being substituted by ChatGPT, and with connectors enabling real-world actions (not just search), operations are migrating to chat. He frames it as: if AI apps are the new browsers, ChatGPT hosts are the new websites—and like websites, they return UI through MCP Apps. He issues a call to action: companies should ship MCP App versions of their dashboards so users can interact inside their preferred chat host rather than visiting separate products.
whyItMatters: The talk connects its engineering abstractions, implementation choices, and AI/product implications into one practical system view.

sections.title: Introduction and Manufact Overview
sections.summary: Pietro Zullo introduces himself as co-founder of Manufact, which builds open-source MCPUs SDKs (8M+ downloads, 10K GitHub stars) and Manifold Cloud for shipping MCP servers. He outlines the talk: MCP app primitives, distribution/discovery mechanisms, and why this is how all software will be used.

sections.title: History and Timeline of MCP Apps
sections.summary: Traces the evolution: MCP launched 2024, MCPUI proposed by Idel Solomon in May 2025 for MCP servers returning UI components, ChatGPT released an app SDK, and by January 2026 MCPUI became the official MCP Apps extension. Character AI and Claude silently opened MCP stores at end of 2025, initially gated behind design partners but now increasingly accepting public submissions.

sections.title: MCP App Architecture Basics
sections.summary: Explains how MCP apps work: the host owns tools, the MCP server returns a widget in a sandboxed iframe instead of JSON, and bidirectional communication occurs between the iframe and host via declared ui:// resources populated with tool arguments. UI organizes information more readably than walls of text.

sections.title: MCP App Primitives and Advanced Features
sections.summary: Covers core primitives: set state (UI updates model context without a user message), UI message (widget sends follow-up messages back to the conversation, with client-specific behavior—Claude shows in chat input for approval, OpenAI auto-sends), incremental streaming UI updates (UI reacts as tool input tokens stream in live, demoed with Remotion video rendering and SVG apps), tool calling from widgets, and data redaction (rich UI shown to user while only sanitized output sent to model).

sections.title: Data Redaction Patterns, Display Modes, and Minor Primitives
sections.summary: Continues data redaction: common pattern shows full info in UI while instructing the model with text about what the user sees, enabling private experiences where LLM data sharing isn't possible. Introduces display modes—inline (default), fullscreen (entire chat becomes widget with input overlaid, useful for video editing), and picture-in-picture. Minor primitives include opening external links from widgets and OS theme synchronization.

sections.title: Live MCP App Demos and Client Support
sections.summary: Shows real MCP apps running in production clients: Cursor with Pulsar MCP displaying analytics UI, Claude with Excalidraw MCP streaming mermaid syntax tokens into a canvas, and ChatGPT with Manifold MCP showing analytics with better rendering. Client support spans ChatGPT, Claude (Co-work, Desktop), Cursor (agent mode, side chat), VS Code, and others. Builders can detect client capabilities via metadata exchange to conditionally return UI elements only for compatible hosts.

sections.title: Building MCP Apps with MCPUs SDK
sections.summary: Explains MCPUs SDK development pattern: design MCP server conventionally with tools, return React widget components from a resources folder automatically registered as UI resources, compiled to HTML/CSS and linked to tools. Template available via `npx create MCP app`. SDK helps detect whether connected client supports MCP apps.

sections.title: Distribution, Discovery, and Market Significance
sections.summary: Covers self-serve stores on ChatGPT, Claude (team/enterprise), and Cursor with different submission processes and speeds. Submission involves linking remote MCP server, tool scanning for correct annotations, authentication checks, test cases, and manual/automated testing. Manufact assists at manifactory.com with vetting and submission artifacts. One-click install URLs replace JSON config sharing. Claude currently performs dynamic discovery—searching MCP registry for the right connector when no specific tool matches—with ChatGPT expected to follow, creating high-intent discovery across 1B+ users. Pietro shares personal workflow using Granola MCP, Linear, and Claude Code, and cites Paul Graham: 'AI apps are the new browsers.'

sections.title: Closing Argument and Call to Action
sections.summary: Pietro extends Paul Graham's framing: Google Search is already being substituted by ChatGPT, and with connectors enabling real-world actions (not just search), operations are migrating to chat. He argues that if AI apps are the new browsers, ChatGPT hosts are the new websites—and like websites they return UI through MCP Apps. He issues a call to action: companies should ship MCP App versions of their dashboards so users can interact inside their preferred chat host. He thanks the audience and opens for questions.

demonstrations: Three-articles demo showing set state: UI displays articles, model initially knows nothing is selected, user modifies UI state and the change is communicated to the model via set state primitive
Shoe example (Trey Blazer Pro) showing UI message: a 'learn more' button in the widget sends a follow-up message back into the chat conversation
Remotion MCP app: renders a video built with React inside the widget in real time as the model streams input tokens into tool arguments
SVG rendering MCP app using incremental streaming UI updates pattern
Tool calling from widget: a button in the UI triggers another tool call to gather additional data from the MCP server

Data redaction example: rich UI card shown to user with private information while model only receives sanitized text or nothing, with a text note that the user is seeing private info in the widget above
Cursor demo with Pulsar MCP showing analytics UI element alongside code editing
Claude demo with Excalidraw MCP server streaming mermaid syntax tokens into a canvas widget that updates live
ChatGPT demo with Manifold MCP app showing analytics with better rendering than Cursor
limitations: Client behaviors vary across hosts for features like UI message—Claude requires user approval, OpenAI auto-sends—meaning builders must account for inconsistent UX
MCP stores were initially gated behind design partnerships, only recently opening to broader submissions
Submission processes and speeds differ across stores, with Claude being slower for now
Only Claude currently performs dynamic discovery; ChatGPT is expected to follow but timing is uncertain
Client support varies—some clients do more, some do less with MCP app features
Many companies and developers still don't understand what MCP Apps are or how to build and distribute them
